lem-qc-countable-compact-null-union:
## Statement

Let $m\ge1$ and let $(K_i)_{i\ge0}$ be a sequence of compact null subsets of $\mathbb R^m$, where nullity is in the closed-cube-cover sense of [[def-null-and-content-zero-in-rn]]. Then $\bigcup_{i\ge0}K_i$ is null. The proof selects finite rational-cube covers by their least codes and uses no choice principle.
lem-qc-open-cube-is-not-null:
## Statement

For every integer $m\ge1$, every nonempty open subset $O\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ is not null in the closed-cube-cover sense of [[def-null-and-content-zero-in-rn]]. The proof uses no choice principle.
def-qc-projective-chord-distance:
## Definition

For an integer $D\ge1$ and unit vectors $u,v\in\mathbb C^D$, write $[u]$ and $[v]$ for their pure-state rays and define the projective chord distance by

$$d_{\mathrm{ch}}([u],[v])=\inf_{|\lambda|=1}\|u-\lambda v\|_2.$$

Here $\|\cdot\|_2$ is the norm induced by the root inner product, which is linear in its first argument. The infimum is over unit complex scalars, so it removes only the common phase of a state vector. The companion lemma [[lem-qc-projective-chord-distance-formula]] evaluates this infimum, proves it is attained, gives the closed formula, and proves independence from the chosen unit representatives.
def-qc-projective-space-atlas:
## Definition

For an integer $D\ge1$, let $\mathbb{CP}^{D-1}$ be the quotient of $\mathbb C^D\setminus\{0\}$ by $z\sim w$ when $w=\lambda z$ for a nonzero complex scalar $\lambda$. Give $\mathbb C^D\setminus\{0\}$ its usual Euclidean topology and the quotient the topology in which a subset is open exactly when its inverse image is open. Every nonzero ray has a unit representative, and two unit representatives of one ray differ by a unit scalar, so this is the pure-state ray space of [[def-qc-pure-state-and-ray]].

For $j\in\{0,\ldots,D-1\}$ define the standard patch $U_j=\{[z]\in\mathbb{CP}^{D-1}:z_j\ne0\}$ and the candidate coordinate map $\phi_j([z])=(z_i/z_j)_{i\ne j}$, with the coordinates kept in increasing original index order. Its candidate inverse sends $w\in\mathbb C^{D-1}$ to the ray of the vector with $j$th coordinate $1$ and other coordinates given by $w$ in that same order. [[thm-qc-projective-chart-dimension]] proves these are smooth charts, computes their real dimension, and notes that a single standard patch omits part of projective space when $D\ge2$.
lem-qc-projective-chord-distance-formula:
## Statement

For unit vectors $u,v\in\mathbb C^D$,

$$d_{\mathrm{ch}}([u],[v])=\sqrt{2-2|\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}|}.$$

In particular, this value is independent of the chosen unit representatives, and it is zero exactly when the two vectors represent the same ray.
thm-qc-projective-chart-dimension:
## Statement

For every integer $D\ge1$, the standard patches $U_j$ of [[def-qc-projective-space-atlas]] are smooth charts with coordinate space $\mathbb C^{D-1}=\mathbb R^{2D-2}$. If $D\ge2$, each fixed patch is proper, so a single standard coordinate patch does not cover all of $\mathbb{CP}^{D-1}$.
lem-qc-signed-ray-packing-code:
## Statement

Let $D\ge2$ be an even integer and let $\delta\in\mathbb R$ satisfy $0<\delta<1/4$. There is a family of at least $\exp(c_\delta D)$ unit sign vectors in $\mathbb C^D$, with their first $D/2$ coordinates fixed at $1/\sqrt D$, such that the projective chord distance between distinct resulting rays is at least $2\sqrt\delta$. Here $c_\delta=(\ln2/2)(1-H_2(2\delta))>0$ and $H_2(t)=-t\log_2t-(1-t)\log_2(1-t)$.
def-qc-clean-ancilla-output-projection:
## Definition

Let $n,a\ge0$ be integers and $D=2^n$. Let the data and workspace registers have ordered computational spaces $\mathbb C^D$ and $\mathbb C^{2^a}$, with the ordered tensor factors and product basis of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]]. For a circuit unitary $U$ on their tensor product, its all-zero-workspace projection on a fixed input $|0^n\rangle|0^a\rangle$ is

$$v=(I_D\otimes\langle0^a|)U(|0^n\rangle\otimes|0^a\rangle)\in\mathbb C^D.$$

The projected joint vector is $v\otimes|0^a\rangle$. An exact clean-workspace output on this input means that the full, unconditional output equals $\lambda|\psi\rangle\otimes|0^a\rangle$ for a unit data vector $\psi$ and a unit scalar $\lambda$; then $v=\lambda\psi$. A merely nonzero $v$ defines only the zero-workspace projection branch and does not assert that the workspace is deterministically clean.
def-qc-state-preparation-cost-model:
## Definition

Fix an integer $n\ge0$ and $D=2^n$. An explicit amplitude-table input is a list of $D$ exact complex numbers $(a_x)_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}$ in the ordered basis convention of [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]; it is valid when $\sum_x|a_x|^2=1$. Its target is the pure-state ray $[a]$ under [[def-qc-pure-state-and-ray]]: nonzero scalar multiples represent the same ray, and $a$ is a unit representative when the table is normalized. A claim must state whether its output error is projective chord distance [[def-qc-projective-chord-distance]] or a representative-level vector error.

The cost record keeps these quantities separate: (1) the classical encoding length and table-reading/preprocessing work; (2) continuous-angle gate occurrences, or finite-alphabet gate occurrences when that model is specified; (3) width, clean-workspace and serial-depth usage; and (4) the declared output-error metric. If an encoding assigns exactly $b$ bits to each real coordinate and $b$ bits to each imaginary coordinate, with basis order implicit, the dense table contains exactly $2Db$ input bits. Those bits must decode to the input table in an exact-table claim; finite-precision approximations are separate inputs with separate error hypotheses. An explicit table is classical input: this definition grants no coherent table oracle, QRAM, or free loading operation. Ideal exact complex arithmetic and finite-precision bit cost are distinct models.
alg-qc-isometry-unitary-completion:
## Definition

**Input.** Integers $1\le D\le M$, ordered orthonormal bases of $\mathbb C^D$ and $\mathbb C^M$, and an exact $M\times D$ matrix $V$ whose columns are orthonormal, so $V$ represents a linear isometry in the convention of [[def-linear-isometry-and-orthogonal-or-unitary-operator]]. Arithmetic is ideal exact complex arithmetic with conjugation, norms, square roots, and exact zero tests; no bit-time bound is part of this procedure.

**Procedure.** Initialize an ordered list $L$ with the $D$ columns of $V$. For $j=0,1,\ldots,M-1$, compute

$$r_j=e_j-\sum_{w\in L}\langle e_j,w\rangle_{\mathrm{root}}w.$$

If $\|r_j\|_2=0$, leave $L$ unchanged. Otherwise append $r_j/\|r_j\|_2$ to $L$. After the finite loop, return the square matrix $W$ whose columns are the final list, and return INVALID if the input dimensions or orthonormal-column condition fail.

For integer widths $0\le n\le w$, put $D=2^n$, $M=2^w$, and $a=w-n$. The input data and clean workspace use the ordered tensor-register convention of [[def-qc-tensor-register-and-permutation]] and the big-endian basis encoding of [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]. A clean workspace register starts at $|0^a\rangle$ under [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]]. Let $\Pi$ be the ordered wire permutation that swaps the $n$-wire data block with the $a$-wire zero-workspace block, so $\Pi(|x\rangle|0^a\rangle)=|0^a\rangle|x\rangle$. This sends the declared clean-input basis to the first $D$ standard basis vectors. The matrix $W\Pi$ is the full-unitary extension interface used by [[thm-qc-isometry-completion-and-synthesis]].
alg-qc-state-preparation:
## Definition

**Input and output.** Input an integer $n\ge0$ and an explicit exact table $(a_x)_{x\in\{0,1\}^n}$ in the ordered basis convention of [[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]]. If the table length is not $D=2^n$ or $\sum_x|a_x|^2\ne1$, return INVALID. Otherwise return a finite continuous-gate circuit which prepares the ray $[a]$ from $|0^n\rangle$, together with its classical angle table. When the table is supplied as a dense fixed-width bit encoding, read all $b$ bits of each real and imaginary coordinate before computation. Arithmetic is ideal and exact: it supplies complex arithmetic, absolute value, exact zero tests and square roots; for $x,y\ge0$ not both zero, $\operatorname{atan2}(y,x)$ returns the unique $\phi\in[0,\pi/2]$ with $\cos\phi=x/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$ and $\sin\phi=y/\sqrt{x^2+y^2}$. For $z\ne0$, $\arg z\in(-\pi,\pi]$ is the unique principal angle in the polar form of [[thm-polar-form-with-unique-principal-argument]], so $z=|z|e^{i\arg z}$ by [[cor-complex-exponential-cartesian-form-modulus-and-eulers-identity]]. No Turing bit-time bound is asserted.

**Prefix norms and rotations.** For every binary prefix $p$ of length at most $n$, set

$$r_p=\sqrt{\sum_{x\text{ extends }p}|a_x|^2}.$$

For $\theta\in\mathbb R$ define

$$R_y(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)&-\sin(\theta/2)\\\sin(\theta/2)&\cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}$$

in basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$. This is the $y$-axis rotation in the QC07 exponent convention; [[thm-qc-axis-rotation-pauli-formula]] gives this matrix and its unitarity. Define $C(U)=\operatorname{diag}(I_2,U)$ with the control as the first wire, following [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]]. For each $l=0,\ldots,n-1$ and each length-$l$ prefix $p$ in lexicographic order, skip the operation if $r_p=0$; otherwise set $\theta_p=2\operatorname{atan2}(r_{p1},r_{p0})$ and apply $R_y(\theta_p)$ to bit $l$, controlled on the first $l$ bits equaling $p$. Length zero means no control. Thus no division is performed on a zero-norm branch.

**Exact bounded-arity control construction.** For a control pattern with $m\ge2$ bits, conjugate each zero-control bit by $X$ so the desired condition becomes all ones. Allocate $m-1$ clean work bits $w_1,\ldots,w_{m-1}$. Compute $w_1=c_1c_2$ with one Toffoli; for $j=3,\ldots,m$, compute $w_{j-1}=w_{j-2}c_j$ with one Toffoli. Use the final work bit as the control for the desired two-wire unitary, then apply the Toffolis in reverse order and undo the $X$ conjugations. For a leaf phase, apply $P_\phi=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\phi})$ to the final work bit instead. For $m=1$ use the corresponding one-control unitary directly; for $m=0$ apply the one-qubit operation directly. The work bits return to zero after each operation and are reused. A one-bit leaf phase uses $P_\phi$ directly for pattern $1$ and $XP_\phi X$ for pattern $0$.

**Leaf phases.** For a basis string $x$, define $P_{x,\phi}=I+(e^{i\phi}-1)|x\rangle\langle x|$. Let $x_*$ be the lexicographically first index with $a_{x_*}\ne0$. Put $\phi_*=\arg(a_{x_*})$. For each other $x$ with $a_x\ne0$, put $\phi_x=\arg(a_x)-\phi_*$ and, unless $\phi_x\equiv0\pmod{2\pi}$, apply $P_{x,\phi_x}$ using the control construction above. The reference leaf needs no phase, and zero entries and zero relative phases require no gate. Every nonzero output amplitude is then $e^{-i\phi_*}a_x$, including the reference leaf, so the output is the target ray. When $n=0$, the valid table has one unit-modulus entry and the empty circuit already prepares its unique ray.
thm-qc-continuous-parameter-state-prepar:
## Statement

Let integer $n\ge1$, $D=2^n$, integer workspace count $a\ge0$, and total width $W=n+a$. Fix integers $k\ge1$ and $p\ge1$ and a countable library of gate families of arity at most $k$, each represented by a countable atlas of $C^\infty$ parameter charts that are open subsets of $\mathbb R^q$ with integer $q$ satisfying $0\le q\le p$. For a nonnegative integer gate budget $g$, each circuit topology selects at most $g$ such gates and wire placements; its gate matrices depend smoothly on their parameters. For each fixed topology and parameter-chart tuple, its denotation is the ordered product of the corresponding fixed local gate embeddings, with each embedding acting on its assigned ordered tensor factors and as the identity on the remaining wires, as specified by [[def-qc-circuit-denotational-semantics]]. Circuits act on the fixed input $|0^n\rangle|0^a\rangle$ and exactly prepare a target unit data vector with declared workspace output $\lambda|\psi\rangle|0^a\rangle$ for a unit scalar $\lambda$. In every standard chart of $\mathbb{CP}^{D-1}$, the exactly preparable rays obtainable with at most $g$ gates form a null set whenever $pg<2D-2$. Thus they cannot cover all rays. For fixed $p$, in each standard chart all rays outside a null coordinate subset require at least $\lceil(2D-2)/p\rceil$ gates. Thus almost every target in chart coordinates has exact preparation cost $\Omega(D)$.
thm-qc-finite-width-topology-count:
## Statement

Fix integers $W\ge1$, $A\ge1$, $k\ge1$, and $g\ge0$, and an ordered-wire circuit model with a finite gate alphabet of size $A$ and maximum arity $k$. A serial length-$g$ description is an ordered list of $g$ gate labels and ordered tuples of at most $k$ distinct wire positions; its denotation is the ordered product of the corresponding local gate embeddings. Each parallel layer consists of pairwise wire-disjoint occurrences and denotes their product. With $C_k=k+1$, the number of length-$g$ serial descriptions is at most $(C_k A W^k)^g$. Any parallel circuit with $g$ total occurrences has a serial ordering with the same gate count and denotation.
lem-qc-prefix-norm-rotation-identities:
## Statement

For a prefix $p$ with $0\le |p|<n$ and $r_p>0$, the angle $\theta_p=2\operatorname{atan2}(r_{p1},r_{p0})$ in [[alg-qc-state-preparation]] satisfies

$$\cos(\theta_p/2)=r_{p0}/r_p,\qquad \sin(\theta_p/2)=r_{p1}/r_p.$$
thm-qc-discrete-alphabet-approximate-pre:
## Statement

Fix real numbers $0<\delta<1/4$ and $0\le\varepsilon<\sqrt\delta$. Let integers $n\ge2$, $A\ge1$, $k\ge1$, and $W\ge n$ be fixed, with $D=2^n$, gate-alphabet size $A$, and maximum arity $k$. For an integer gate budget $g\ge0$, every circuit starts on $|0^n\rangle|0^{W-n}\rangle$ and must return the workspace exactly to zero, with its data output within projective chord distance $\varepsilon$ of the target ray. If a circuit family prepares every $D$-dimensional pure-state ray and each circuit in the family has at most $g$ gates in this model, then $g=\Omega(D/\log W)$ as $n\to\infty$, with constants depending on $A,k,\delta,\varepsilon$. In particular, if $W=\operatorname{poly}(n)$, then $g=\Omega(2^n/\log n)$.
thm-qc-finite-alphabet-exact-nonuniversa:
## Statement

Fix integers $n\ge1$, $A\ge0$, $k\ge1$, and $W\ge n$, with $D=2^n$, a gate alphabet of size $A$ and maximum arity $k$. Each circuit starts on $|0^n\rangle|0^{W-n}\rangle$ and is counted as an exact state-preparation circuit only when its unconditional output is $\lambda|\psi\rangle|0^{W-n}\rangle$ for a unit scalar $\lambda$ and a unit data vector $\psi\in\mathbb C^D$. The set of data rays exactly reachable by finite circuits is countable, so it is not the full ray space.
thm-qc-isometry-completion-and-synthesis:
## Statement

For integers $1\le D\le M$, every exact isometry $V:\mathbb C^D\to\mathbb C^M$ is completed by [[alg-qc-isometry-unitary-completion]] to a unitary matrix $W$ whose first $D$ columns are those of $V$. If integers $0\le n\le w$ satisfy $D=2^n$ and $M=2^w$, the full unitary $W\Pi$ acts as $V$ on the clean-input subspace $|x\rangle|0^{w-n}\rangle$. By the exact QSD theorem [[thm-qc-exact-arbitrary-unitary-qsd-upper-bound]], for $w\ge2$ this uses at most $\frac{23}{48}4^w-\frac32 2^w+\frac43$ CNOT gates plus one-qubit gates; for $w=0$ or $w=1$ the small-width cases use no CNOT gates. It does not synthesize $W$ and an extra permutation circuit separately. The $M$ output coordinates are retained: extra output wires may contain part of the encoded state and are not required to return to zero. No classical synthesis bit-time bound is asserted.
thm-qc-state-preparation-rotation-level-:
## Statement

For an integer $n\ge0$, $D=2^n$, and a normalized explicit amplitude table, [[alg-qc-state-preparation]] exactly prepares the target ray using at most $D-1$ prefix rotations and at most $D$ leaf phases. The specified Toffoli flag chain expands each operation into $O(n+1)$ bounded-arity gates using at most $\max\{n-1,0\}$ reusable clean work bits, so the complete circuit has $O((n+1)D)$ gates and serial depth, in addition to the $n$ data qubits. For $n=0$, the ray is trivial and no gate is needed.
thm-qc-amplitude-table-precision-and-com:
## Statement

Let integer $n\ge0$, $D=2^n$, unit vector $a\in\mathbb C^D$, and integer $b\ge1$ be given. Let $v\in\mathbb Q(i)^D$ have each real and imaginary coordinate within $2^{-b}$ of the corresponding coordinate of $a$. Put $\eta=\sqrt{2D}\,2^{-b}$ and assume $\eta<1/2$. Then $v\ne0$ and $\|v/\|v\|_2-a\|_2\le2\eta$. For $n=0$, the unique data ray is prepared by the empty circuit with zero error. For $n\ge1$, prepare the normalized table $v/\|v\|_2$ by [[alg-qc-state-preparation]], and suppose its exact continuous circuit has an integer $G\ge1$ bounded-arity unitary blocks on the data and an integer $s\ge0$ clean work qubits, with $G=O((n+1)D)$. For any $0<\varepsilon_c<1/2$, choose a rational internal budget $\varepsilon'_c$ with $\varepsilon_c/2<\varepsilon'_c<\varepsilon_c$ and compile each complete, unconditional block with projective operator-norm error at most $\varepsilon'_c/G$. Then the compiled joint output ray is within projective chord distance $2\eta+\varepsilon_c$ of $[a\otimes|0^s\rangle]$.

For fixed block arity, the declared compiler interface yields $O(G\log^c(G/\varepsilon_c))$ finite-alphabet gates, with $c=\log_{3/2}5$. If the rational table $v$ is supplied in a dense fixed-width encoding with $b$ bits per real/imaginary coordinate, it has $2Db=\Theta(Db)$ input bits; the preprocessing reads this encoding and computes the exact normalization internally. Table input and preprocessing are separate from coherent gate cost. The statement asserts no uniform bit-time for angle computation or SK compilation; the separate proposed supplier [[thm-qc-solovay-kitaev-bit-complexity]] and certified angle evaluation remain held obligations.
thm-qc-state-preparation-cost:
## Statement

For an integer $n\ge0$, $D=2^n$, and target amplitudes supplied by the explicit normalized amplitude-table model of [[def-qc-state-preparation-cost-model]], [[alg-qc-state-preparation]] reads the dense table and produces an exact target ray using $D-1$ variable-control rotations and at most $D$ phases. The local clean Toffoli ladder yields $O((n+1)D)$ bounded-arity gates and serial depth using at most $\max\{n-1,0\}$ clean work bits in addition to the data register. If an integer $b\ge1$ specifies a dense fixed-width table with $b$ bits for each real and imaginary coordinate that decodes exactly to the input amplitudes, it contains $2Db=\Theta(Db)$ input bits; this procedure's explicit full-table preprocessing scan reads those bits. The statement assumes neither QRAM nor exact arbitrary-angle implementation in a fixed finite gate alphabet. It gives no uniform bit-time bound.
